Theme: Caregivers accept agent coordination that remains selective and accountable
Organizing concept: Caregivers accept the agent when it follows care roles, intervenes selectively, exposes uncertainty, and leaves medication authority with people.
How it addresses the care gap: Role-sensitive reminders and information reach the person already responsible for the next medication task.
Boundary and variation: The responsible person differs across household routines; prescription and stock features were not deployed.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; direction; C2 and C3

Theme: Caregivers accept agent coordination that remains selective and accountable
Organizing concept: Caregivers accept the agent when it follows care roles, intervenes selectively, exposes uncertainty, and leaves medication authority with people.
How it addresses the care gap: Retry, time, consent, and a selected relative make family involvement proportional to an unresolved event.
Boundary and variation: Continuous updates or unrelated information exceed the agent's accepted mandate.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; visibility, revocability, and ceremony; C2 and C3

Theme: Caregivers accept agent coordination that remains selective and accountable
Organizing concept: Caregivers accept the agent when it follows care roles, intervenes selectively, exposes uncertainty, and leaves medication authority with people.
Sub-theme: Exceptions focus caregiver attention without claiming adherence
How it addresses the care gap: Selective alerts direct attention to ambiguous events without treating nonconfirmation as proof of a missed dose.
Boundary and variation: False or unexplained alerts recreate vigilance and spread worry.

Theme: Caregivers accept agent coordination that remains selective and accountable
Organizing concept: Caregivers accept the agent when it follows care roles, intervenes selectively, exposes uncertainty, and leaves medication authority with people.
How it addresses the care gap: Prescriptions, clinicians, family checking, fallback, and revocation keep coordination accountable to people.
Boundary and variation: The agent can coordinate an authorized routine but cannot prescribe, change medicine, or replace care.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; tool and advocate boundaries; C2 and C3

Theme: Caregivers interpret streaks as records of routine care work
Organizing concept: Caregivers interpret the streak as a visible record of quiet coordination while refusing to treat it as medication motivation.
How it addresses the care gap: A limited family view makes sustained scheduling, prompting, confirming, and checking recognizable as caregiving work.
Boundary and variation: The trace represents only care recorded through the prototype and does not prove ingestion.
RQ and contribution: RQ3; visibility and caregiver recognition; C3

Theme: Caregivers interpret streaks as records of routine care work
Organizing concept: Caregivers interpret the streak as a visible record of quiet coordination while refusing to treat it as medication motivation.
Sub-theme: Medicine remains independent of the score
How it addresses the care gap: Caregivers investigate whether medicine or confirmation was missed and continue the routine regardless of the score.
Boundary and variation: Pressure, blame, competition, anxiety, or wider disclosure makes the score unacceptable.
RQ and contribution: RQ3; dignity and gamification boundary; C3
